summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, set up a worktree and tried `sdd-state claim` on tasks 1 and 2. Both came back status=held, exit=4. It then asked whether to take a task over, I said no, and it handed back. It never ran `sdd-state next`, `sdd-state wait --kind tasks` or `sdd-state board`, and no waiting record was written. So the empty-frontier rule was not followed. It also did not take over any task.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 failed. The agent never ran `sdd-state next`, `wait --kind tasks` or `board`, and no waiting/ file exists on disk. It did load the skill first, did not take over a task, and handed back saying both tasks are held by fixture-session. The core thing this scenario tests, the empty-frontier rule (post a waiting record, print the board, hand back), was not followed.

observations.description: The skill's empty-frontier path was not followed. Instead of `sdd-state next`, then `sdd-state wait --kind tasks`, then `sdd-state board`, the agent tried `sdd-state claim` on each task one at a time. When both came back held it asked the user about a takeover. No waiting record was posted, so the other session cannot see that this session is waiting.

The agent appended a session line to progress.md by hand with a `cat >> $W/progress.md` heredoc, writing straight into the cache state directory instead of using an sdd-state verb. If the skill expects state changes to go through sdd-state, this bypasses it.

The agent asked about a takeover (an AskUserQuestion with 4 options) before posting a wait or showing the board. When every task is held, the skill should probably post the waiting record and hand back rather than ask first.
The first command in the log is a compound Bash command that ran `sdd-state sync` and `sdd-dir` together, then the agent reran each one separately. The commands are redundant.

Startup friction: on the workspace trust and bypass-permissions dialogs the cursor starts on 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt also appeared even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5 (it said the pinned model was Opus 5).

The new worktree was created on branch `worktree-parallel` (via EnterWorktree), not on the plan's registered branch feature/parallel. That may be intended for joining sessions, but it is worth checking.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development skill before any other work
criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in session log aa8b75ef-...jsonl is `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`, and the screen shows "Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" before anything else.

criteria.criterion: Ran `sdd-state next` and output shows `none reason=held`
criteria.evidence: I extracted the Bash commands from the log with jq and grepped them for `sdd-state (next|wait|board)`: 0 matches. The agent probed with `sdd-state claim ... 1` and `... 2` instead. Their output was `status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ... exit=4` (same for task 2).

criteria.criterion: Posted waiting record of kind tasks (command + file under waiting/ with kind=tasks)
criteria.evidence: There is no `sdd-state wait` command in the transcript (grep count 0). `find $HOME/.cache -path '*waiting*'` returned nothing. The plan state dir parallel-43d696ad has only progress.md and claims/task-1, claims/task-2.
Grepping the Bash commands for `sdd-state board` found 0 matches.

criteria.criterion: Handed back saying every task is held by another session
criteria.evidence: Before asking, the agent said: "Both tasks in parallel.md are already claimed by your other session, fixture-session, so there's nothing for me to pick up yet." Its final message was: "I'll leave both claims with fixture-session and dispatch nothing... Tell me when you want this session to do something." The prompt then came back idle.

criteria.criterion: Did not take over a held task (no --takeover)
criteria.evidence: Grepping the log's Bash commands for `--takeover` returned 0. The only claim attempts had no --takeover and were refused with exit=4.
